slides.say: A B C D is an isosceles trapezoid. A D is parallel to B C, A D is five centimeters and B C is twenty centimeters. The shaded triangle A B D has an area of fifteen square centimeters. What is the area of the trapezoid?
at: A B C D is an isosceles trapezoid

slides.say: We know the area of the shaded triangle, and we need the area of the whole trapezoid. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways. First the math way, and then by understanding, with equal heights.
[short pause] The math way first. The shaded part is a triangle, an obtuse one. Its area is base times height, over two, and the only base we know is A D, five.
at: the only base we know is A D

slides.say: Where is the height to A D? For this base, A D, the perpendicular from B lands beyond A. So we extend D A past A, and from B we draw the perpendicular to that line. Its length, the perpendicular distance, is the height h.
at: So we extend D A past A
from B we draw the perpendicular

slides.say: So five times h, over two, is fifteen. Multiply both sides by two, and five h is thirty. Divide by five, so h is six.
And look, this height is also the height of the trapezoid, the distance between the two parallel sides. The area of a trapezoid is the sum of the bases, times the height, over two.
at: this height is also the height of the trapezoid

slides.say: Five plus twenty is twenty-five. Twenty-five times six is a hundred fifty. And a hundred fifty over two is seventy-five. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now by understanding, using equal heights. Look at the shaded triangle A B D and the white triangle B C D. They have the same height, the distance between the parallel sides. For B C D, it's the perpendicular from D down to B C. For A B D, it's the perpendicular from B to the line of A D.

When two triangles have the same height, the ratio of their areas is the ratio of their bases. The shaded base is five, and the white base is twenty, four times bigger. So the white area is four times bigger too.
at: When two triangles have the same height

slides.say: Let's see it. Cut B C into four pieces of five, and draw lines from D. Now every triangle here has the same base, five, and the same height. A B and the first piece even make a parallelogram, with B D as its diagonal.
at: Cut B C into four pieces

slides.say: So all the triangles have the same area, fifteen each. The four small white ones make four times fifteen, sixty. The whole trapezoid is the shaded fifteen plus sixty, which is seventy-five. Choice number three again. Careful, sixty is only the white triangle, so choice number two is a trap.
at: The whole trapezoid is the shaded
choice number two is a trap

slides.say: So when two triangles have the same perpendicular height, the area ratio is the base ratio. If the base were three times bigger, the area would be three times bigger. We didn't use that the trapezoid is isosceles, so this works for any trapezoid with these bases and this area. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
